penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: SEO recovery involves nuanced diagnosis per site — Google's indexing behaviour is opaque and inconsistent, and affected business owners will ask 'why isn't it working yet?' questions that require human judgement to answer credibly.

rationale: The buyer is specific and commercially motivated — small SaaS and business site owners who depend on organic traffic and have just lost it — and pain severity is high (direct revenue loss). Willingness to pay is credible given the revenue impact. However, the pain is low-frequency (most sites are deindexed rarely or once), which limits recurring revenue potential. The total of 5.3 falls just below the validate threshold of 5.5, and the autonomy score of 6 only barely clears its build gate floor. The deciding factor is frequency: a deindexing event is a crisis, not a steady subscription need, making the unit economics difficult for a recurring SaaS.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be an 'SEO Deindex Recovery Audit' — a paid one-time report (e.g. $97-$197) where the owner submits their site URL and a brief description of the incident, Claude analyzes their Search Console data (exported as CSV), checks technical signals (sitemap validity, crawl errors, redirect chains, canonical tags), and produces a prioritized recovery checklist with exact Search Console actions to take. The factory builds this as a Tally intake form + Claude analysis prompt + automated PDF report delivered by email + a Stripe payment link. No coding by Youval. To sell: reach out to site owners posting in SEO forums (WebmasterWorld, r/SEO, StackExchange) and to SaaS founders on Twitter/X who mention deindexing — outreach drafts are queued for Youval's approval before sending. Maintenance is mostly automated; Youval only approves outreach batches. The main limit is that demand is event-driven and sporadic, making it a one-off product rather than a subscription — viable as a side earner but not a scalable recurring business.
notes: Total 5.3 falls below min_total_to_validate (5.5) — drop. If frequency were higher (e.g. bundled with ongoing monitoring), the score would clear validate. Worth revisiting as a one-time report product if a higher-volume lead channel is identified.
